Robotics engineering / pose-graph construction

TRACE.

Building g2o pose graphs with and without ROS, identifying loop closures with Scan Context and PY-ICP, and reconstructing and verifying trajectories from the resulting graphs.

g2oROS / ROS-freeScan ContextPY-ICPLoop ClosureTrajectory Verification
01 / Objective

From measurements to a verifiable pose graph.

TRACE is an end-to-end workflow for constructing pose-graph files in .g2o format, whether the source data is processed through ROS or through a ROS-independent workflow.

The essential challenge is not just plotting a trajectory: it is assembling poses and relative constraints, identifying loop closures, and checking that the resulting graph produces a coherent trajectory.

Can we build g2o graphs in both workflows, detect and refine loop closures, and verify the trajectories they produce?
02 / Pipeline

Two paths to one graph format.

ROS-based and ROS-free processing paths feed into the same goal: a pose graph with motion constraints and loop-closure constraints, exported as a .g2o file.

Conceptual workflow. The loop-closure constraints are incorporated into the pose graph; the arrows summarize the stages rather than prescribing an exact software execution order.

03 / Implementation

Graph generation, loop closure, uncertainty, verification.

A / Graph generation

ROS and ROS-free .g2o

Construct and export pose-graph vertices and constraints through both processing paths.

B / Loop closures

Scan Context + PY-ICP

Identify loop-closure candidates with Scan Context and use PY-ICP for geometric alignment of candidate pairs.

C / Registration uncertainty

FAST-LIO + ICP covariance

Examine uncertainty associated with FAST-LIO-derived motion estimates and scan registration. Compare point-to-point and point-to-plane ICP residual models; investigate Censi-style covariance estimation for registration constraints.

D / Verification

Trajectory reconstruction

Build trajectories from the graph and inspect their geometry, elevation profiles and consecutive step sizes.

Constraint quality / measurement uncertainty

From registration residuals to graph information

FAST-LIO provides a LiDAR–inertial odometry trajectory that can support pose-graph construction. For loop-closure registration, point-to-point ICP penalizes 3D correspondence distances, whereas point-to-plane ICP penalizes displacement along local surface normals. The residual model affects how registration uncertainty should be estimated.

Motion estimates

FAST-LIO

LiDAR–inertial poses and relative-motion constraints.

Registration

Point ↔ point / plane

ICP residuals used to align candidate loop closures.

Uncertainty

Censi-style covariance

Study how registration geometry and residual sensitivity inform constraint confidence.

Methodological context: a covariance estimate must be validated before using its inverse as an information matrix in a .g2o edge. This page does not claim a particular estimator was fully implemented or benchmarked.

The deliverable is the pose-graph construction and loop-closure workflow, including attention to measurement uncertainty. Trajectory plots are a way to verify its outputs.
04 / Verification

Verifying the generated trajectories

After constructing the pose graphs and identifying loop closures, the resulting trajectories are inspected in 2D and 3D. The figures below provide checks of path geometry, altitude variation and consecutive-pose displacement for Garage, NCLT and Intel.

KITTI sequence 0018 · RViz visualization

Recorded RViz visualization for KITTI sequence 0018, showing the point-cloud display during the TRACE workflow. This is a qualitative visualization, not a quantitative accuracy benchmark or evidence of a completed loop closure.

Original user-supplied experimental plots, preserved with their axes and legends. Abrupt step-size peaks may be useful to investigate, but the plots alone do not identify their causes.

TRACE connects g2o generation, Scan Context / PY-ICP loop-closure identification, and trajectory verification in ROS and ROS-free workflows.
